text:
maya: Heads up — our release 0.42.1 canary is blocked. perf-ci flagged a regression on the int4 quant profile in the hosted benchmark: ~20% higher p95 token latency and 18% throughput loss. Rolling out paused by release-manager :no_entry:
perf-ci: CI benchmark job r-0.42.1/int4-profile failed: baseline throughput 11.8k t/s -> 9.6k t/s. Attached perf artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1760845123/int4/baseline_vs_head.tar.gz
sam: Ugh. Any suspect merges? I ran a quick git bisect across the last 7 merges and it points at PR #4387 (kernel-selection-refactor). That PR landed with a minor change to the runtime's kernel picker heuristics.
chen: I grabbed a flamegraph from the canary nodes and did a quick profile. The big delta is in the dequant path inside attention kernels — dequantization now happens per-chunk instead of once per sequence when a certain kernel variant is chosen.
chen: snippet from perf output (summarized):
```
old (pre-PR): attention_total = 42% runtime, dequant_step = 6%
new (post-PR): attention_total = 61% runtime, dequant_step = 28%
```
liz: That matches my repro on an A10 instance with the int4 profile. I saw repeated calls to dequantize_tensor() at every KV write during generation. Looks like the kernel variant selected doesn't support fused KV-dequant path so we fall back to a generic path.
maya: Does the kernel selection refactor change fallback ordering or just add a new 'safety' check? If it's choosing a non-fused kernel for certain seq-len/batch combinations that's a regression.
sam: The refactor introduced a cost model tweak: prefer L2-friendly kernels for long heads. But the tuning constants were inverted for small sequences — which is exactly our int4 canary config (seq=128, batch=4). I'm 90% sure this is the culprit.
qa: Can we confirm by forcing the old kernel? e.g. env var `REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=legacy_fused_attn` or a runtime flag? If perf recovers that's a clear repro.
chen: I did that locally. Forcing `legacy_fused_attn` brings throughput back to 12.1k t/s and p95 down 15%. So it's definitely selection-related.
sam: OK, plan: open an emergency revert of the kernel-picker tweak and cut a canary rollback. I'll prepare a revert PR and link the hash here. Also we should add a regression test in CI that runs the int4 perf profile against a small synthetic workload.
sam: Proposed revert commit: `git revert --no-edit b7a3c9f7` (PR coming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4399)
maya: Good. Also we should add a quick mitigation: if kernel chosen causes repeated dequant calls (detect by checking dequant_per_token rate > threshold), prefer fallback to fused kernel automatically. That'll help avoid future perf regressions from heuristic tweaks.
devops-bot: Canary rollout paused for r-0.42.1. Notifying release-manager and tagging `@oncall-release`.
perf-ci: Reran perf job with revert branch (rebased on head). Results: throughput 12.0k t/s (baseline 11.8k), p95 latency slightly improved. Attaching artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1760845123/int4/revert-run.tar.gz
liz: Verified KV cache behavior also normalized — dequant run count reduced by ~80% in flamegraphs. Looks like the fused path was the missing piece.
qa: I'll add the int4 perf check to the perf-suite (short-run) and a unit that asserts dequant_per_token <= 0.05. Will file a follow-up PR.
maya: Thanks everyone. Sam, please merge the revert and coordinate with release to unpause canary once we have a clean run. Add an item to the follow-up to add automatic fuzzing of kernel selector across seq/batch/quant profiles.
sam: Revert PR merged and new perf check opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4401. Notifying release to resume canary when green. :thumbsup:
